terms.name: Abbreviation
terms.definition: A shortened form of a word or phrase, from Dr. to NASA, with its own typographic conventions and an expansion assistive tech can speak.

terms.name: Additive animation
terms.definition: Composing an animation on top of whatever is already animating the same property instead of replacing it, so a second nudge adds to the first rather than restarting it.

terms.name: App shell
terms.definition: The persistent frame of an application, its header, navigation and footer, that stays put while only the content region swaps as you move around.

terms.name: Aurora UI
terms.definition: A style whose background is built from heavily blurred color blobs that glow and drift like the northern lights behind the content.

terms.name: Blockquote
terms.definition: A passage quoted from another source and set off from the running text as its own block, carrying the attribution with it.

terms.name: Button group
terms.definition: Buttons set flush against each other so they read as one unit of related actions, usually with shared borders and rounded outer corners only.

terms.name: Change of context
terms.definition: A shift big enough to disorient a reader, a new page, a new window, a moved focus, a rearranged form, and the rule that it should follow a request rather than a keystroke.

terms.name: Click-through
terms.definition: A click that both focuses an inactive surface and reaches the control underneath, instead of being spent activating the window first.

terms.name: Color role
terms.definition: A named job in the interface, such as surface or outline or on-primary, that components style themselves against instead of reaching for a palette value.

terms.name: Comparison table
terms.definition: A table whose columns are options and whose rows are features, read across to decide between plans or products.

terms.name: Containing block
terms.definition: The box an element's percentages and offsets are measured against, which is not always its parent and changes with how the element is positioned.

terms.name: Current page indicator
terms.definition: The marking of which item in a navigation set is the one you are on, exposed with aria-current so it survives without the colour cue.

terms.name: Deconstructed pancake
terms.definition: A row of equal cards that wraps to fewer per line as space runs out, with the last line left aligned at its natural size rather than stretched to fill.

terms.name: Disclosure
terms.definition: A single button that shows and hides one region of content, reporting its state through aria-expanded.

terms.name: Drag threshold
terms.definition: The small distance a pointer must travel while pressed before the gesture counts as a drag, so a shaky click is not mistaken for one.

terms.name: Easter egg
terms.definition: A reward hidden behind an action nobody was told about, put there to be found rather than to be used.

terms.name: Error message
terms.definition: The line attached to a field that says what went wrong and what to do about it, announced to assistive technology the moment it appears.

terms.name: Fake urgency
terms.definition: Presenting a deadline that does not exist, usually a timer that resets on reload, so the reader hurries a decision they had time to make.

terms.name: Fisheye view
terms.definition: A focus plus context display that magnifies whatever has attention and progressively compresses everything further away, like a lens dragged along a list.

terms.name: Focus delegation
terms.definition: A shadow root option that forwards focus from the host into the first focusable element inside it, so clicking the padding of a custom element does not leave focus nowhere.

terms.name: Font weight
terms.definition: How thick a typeface's strokes are, named in steps from thin to black and numbered from 100 to 900 on the web.

terms.name: Ghost click
terms.definition: A stray click the browser emits after a touch has already been handled, landing on whatever moved under the finger in the meantime.

terms.name: Guest checkout
terms.definition: Letting a buyer complete a purchase without creating an account, with the offer to save details moved to after the order is placed.

terms.name: Hex color
terms.definition: A colour written as a hash followed by three, four, six or eight hexadecimal digits, the notation most handoffs still speak even when the source is OKLCH.

terms.name: Hue shift
terms.definition: Rotating hue deliberately along a ramp, warmer at the light end and cooler at the dark end, so a scale looks alive instead of like one colour fading out.

terms.name: Initial focus
terms.definition: Where focus lands when a view, dialog, or page first appears, chosen deliberately rather than left on the body or dumped on the first close button.

terms.name: Inverted colors
terms.definition: A whole-screen colour inversion applied by the OS, which flips a design nobody tested upside down and turns every shadow into a highlight.

terms.name: Keyboard trap
terms.definition: A place keyboard focus can enter but not leave by keyboard alone, stranding anyone who is not using a pointer.

terms.name: Lazy loading
terms.definition: Deferring the fetch of an image, list section, or module until it is about to be needed, usually when it approaches the viewport.

terms.name: Liquid Glass
terms.definition: Apple's 2025 material where controls float as a translucent layer that refracts what is behind them and reshapes fluidly as content moves underneath.

terms.name: Magic link
terms.definition: Signing in by clicking a single-use link emailed on request, with no password, and a screen that waits and offers to resend while the mail arrives.

terms.name: Menu bar extra
terms.definition: A small application controlled item living in the system menu bar or tray, usually an icon that opens a compact panel of status and controls.

terms.name: Mockup
terms.definition: A screen shown as it will look rather than as it will work: colour, type and real copy all settled, and nothing in it clickable.

terms.name: Multi column layout
terms.definition: An application shell with three or more vertical regions, typically navigation, a list, and a reading pane, as in a mail client.

terms.name: Neutral palette
terms.definition: The greys an interface is mostly made of, ramped from page background to body text, which carry the structure while the accent carries the attention.

terms.name: Onboarding tour
terms.definition: A short sequence of pointers layered over a live interface, each naming one control, advanced by the reader and skippable at any point.

terms.name: Overflow menu
terms.definition: A menu holding the actions that do not fit in the visible interface, opened from one compact trigger.

terms.name: Parallax
terms.definition: Moving layers at different rates against the same input, so the slower layers read as farther away and the scene gains depth.

terms.name: Plain language
terms.definition: Writing interface copy at the reading level of the people using it, with short sentences, familiar words, and the point first, rather than at the level of the org chart.

terms.name: Presentational children
terms.definition: The rule that some roles flatten everything inside them into their own label, which is why an icon and a span inside a button are never announced separately.

terms.name: Property filter
terms.definition: A search field that builds structured queries from tokens, letting a reader filter by named properties with operators rather than free text.

terms.name: RAM technique
terms.definition: A grid that decides its own column count from a minimum item width, so the same one line rule works at every screen size without a single breakpoint.

terms.name: Relative color syntax
terms.definition: CSS notation that builds a new colour from an existing one by naming an origin colour with from and then adjusting individual channels.

terms.name: Roach motel
terms.definition: Making entry into a commitment take one click and exit take a phone call, a chat queue, or a buried page, so the asymmetry keeps people subscribed.

terms.name: Scope bar
terms.definition: The row of category buttons directly under a search field that narrows what the query searches, such as All, Mail, Files.

terms.name: Scrubber
terms.definition: The seek control of a media player: a track showing elapsed and buffered time with a playhead you drag to move through it.

terms.name: Sequential palette
terms.definition: A data palette that runs light to dark in one direction, encoding an ordered quantity so that darker always means more.

terms.name: Skeuomorphism
terms.definition: A style that makes interface elements imitate real objects and materials, using leather, metal, paper, and glossy highlights so their purpose reads as familiar.

terms.name: Soft hyphen
terms.definition: An invisible character placed inside a word that marks where a hyphen may appear if the word has to break, and stays hidden otherwise.

terms.name: Splitter
terms.definition: The draggable bar between two panes that changes how much room each one gets, keyboard operable as a slider between limits.

terms.name: Step indicator
terms.definition: A row or column of numbered stages showing where you are in a multi step flow and what remains.

terms.name: Subtractive colour
terms.definition: Colour made by taking light away, where inks stack towards black and every added layer can only darken, which is why a screen blue cannot be printed.

terms.name: System color keyword
terms.definition: A CSS keyword such as Canvas, CanvasText or LinkText that resolves to a colour chosen by the operating system rather than by the page.

terms.name: Text columns
terms.definition: Flowing one block of running text into several columns that fill and balance automatically, with an optional rule drawn between them.

terms.name: Toast
terms.definition: A brief, self-dismissing message that appears at a screen edge to confirm an action or report status without interrupting the user's flow.

terms.name: Tree select
terms.definition: A select whose popup is a tree, so options can be chosen at any depth with parents collapsing over their children.

terms.name: Undo
terms.definition: Letting an action run immediately and offering to reverse it afterwards, instead of stopping to ask whether the reader really meant it.

terms.name: View transition
terms.definition: An animated change between two states of a page, where the browser photographs before and after and interpolates the elements the two have in common.

terms.name: Windows Aero
terms.definition: The Windows Vista and 7 look built on translucent glass window frames, soft outer glows, reflections, and animated window transitions.
